dedupe_keys.name: isgan mc cba toolkit combined multi criteria cost benefit analysis of smart grid plans with a case study

description: This report presents the MC-CBA toolkit, software that combines multi-criteria analysis with cost-benefit analysis to choose between smart grid investment options, and applies it in a case study. It was prepared in 2018 for the International Smart Grid Action Network (ISGAN) by Working Group 3, with Fabrizio Pilo and Matteo Troncia as authors, and republished on Zenodo. The motive is that smart grid projects have wide impacts, many not easily expressed in money, so classic cost-benefit analysis is unfit, while a hybrid approach keeps the strengths of both methods. The toolkit splits impacts into economic effects, contribution to smart grid realisation and externalities, and ranks alternatives with the Analytic Hierarchy Process in an automated, output-based comparison meant to preserve stakeholders' interests. The case study compares distribution upgrade plans based on the active distribution network approach and on siting and sizing distributed storage. Coverage is a generic distribution network. The report is downloadable from Zenodo as a PDF under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: the toolkit software itself is not in the Zenodo record, and weights depend on stakeholder judgements. Simulation uses are appraising distribution grid investments that improve flexibility and reliability. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
